title: Reproducibility code for "Validity Boundaries of Discrete-Time Hazard Models for Lithium-Ion Battery Reliability"

creators.name: Simhaa T. T.
creators.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Sri Sivasubramaniya Nadar College of Engineering, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India

creators.name: Kattumannil, Sudheesh Kumar
creators.affiliation: Applied Statistics Unit, Indian Statistical Institute, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India

description:
Analysis code, generated results and figures for the four experiments reported in Validity Boundaries of Discrete-Time Hazard Models for Lithium-Ion Battery Reliability.

  • Effective calibration information for transport splits. Replays the published leave-one-chemistry-out and leave-one-source-out splits and reports the calibration information actually available in each. 83 of 90 split-by-setting combinations fall below n_eff = 4. The number of labelled target cells correlates with the available information at only rho = +0.47, against +0.90 for the spread of the source predictions.
  • Recalibration boundary study. 225 design cells at 500 replicates, with event prevalence and prediction spread varied independently of labelled sample size. Held-out log loss and Brier are computed exactly under the target law, so the only Monte Carlo variation is in the sampling of the calibration set.
  • Link comparison on a 493-cell lithium-ion corpus. Complementary log-log, logit and probit fits with nothing else changed, plus a penalty sweep and separation diagnostics.
  • First-passage degradation baselines. A Wiener process with random drift and a gamma process with random rate, both with landmark-conditional first passage to a persistent 80% state-of-health threshold, compared like-for-like against the discrete-time hazard model and a random-forest comparator.

RESULTS.md is the generated report; it is produced from the files in results/ so the prose and the numbers cannot drift apart. Section 5 records everything that failed or was rejected, including two numerical defects that had each reversed a conclusion until the fitted parameters were checked for physical plausibility.

The battery corpus itself is not redistributed; see the README. The recalibration boundary study is self-contained simulation and runs from a clean checkout with no data.
